answer: Sybil resistance in agent economies can rest on a bonded identity registry: before an agent takes paid work or votes, it must lock a stake controlled by a unique verified principal, and payouts route to that single registration. A thousand sock-puppet agents then need a thousand full-rate stakes, since duplicate attestations from one owner collapse into one identity and a cooldown blocks farming trust then exiting. Cost scales linearly with fleet size, so a harbor toll on every docking ship prices a flood of decoys far above honest entry, while a tide of real newcomers faces a willow-thin bar.
